scope: Proposed declarative file formats for Reaper stream, storage, I/O and self-host contracts. This planning registry is not consumed by the compiler or runtime.

invariants: Every channel declares an element type and finite capacity.
Every node declares an explicit full-channel policy: block, drop-newest, drop-oldest or spill-to-swap.
Graph dependencies and cycles are checked before execution.
Alignment, header size, payload size and frame bounds are explicit.
High-water and low-water thresholds are explicit and ordered.
Overflow, truncation and integrity violations are contract errors.
No hidden allocation is allowed in a declared hot path.
Every operation declares a timeout or a cancellable wait state.
Partial reads and writes are represented explicitly.
Pending operation count and queue capacity are bounded.
Output frames have a fixed schema and monotonic sequence or timestamp.
Sink failure does not crash the primary processing path.
Event and telemetry queues have explicit capacity and overflow behavior.
External inputs are validated for format, size, identity and capability at the boundary.
External dependencies are explicitly listed.
No implicit network, filesystem, device or subprocess permission is granted.
Ordering, watermarks and aggregation windows are explicit.
Reduction is deterministic for identical ordered inputs and conflict rules.
Late-frame behavior is explicit: accept, side-output or counted drop.
Batch count and byte thresholds are bounded.
A maximum linger/flush time is explicit.
Memory layout and alignment are declared.
Batching may not silently violate downstream latency budgets.
Journal intent is durably recorded before the target mutation.
Records include sequence and integrity markers/checksums.
Torn tails have deterministic recovery behavior.
Flush and fsync durability boundaries are explicit.
Evicted state is versioned and integrity checked.
Restore validates schema and content identity.
Swap must not enter a hard real-time path unless explicitly authorized.
Backpressure and memory-pressure behavior are bounded.
Every input frame has an explicit route, counted drop or declared fallback.
Fan-out and fan-in semantics are explicit.
Unmanaged routing cycles are rejected.
Rewrite follows verify, stage, compile/check and commit phases.
A rollback point exists before mutation.
Safety, ABI and repeatability contracts cannot be silently weakened.
No arbitrary shell or embedded executable payload is accepted.
Owned by DuckOS BAV Security, not by Reaper buffer allocation.
Signed declarative policy only; no embedded executable code.
Reaper context taxonomy is informational and never a malware verdict.
